plan.primary: One exploratory spread-arrival native-tail characterization: all-request external-arrival mean flow, raw TTFT/completion/max-gap distributions, throughput, failures/unfinished, realized output and EOS. No victim-policy performance contrast and no new SLO.
plan.slo: No application SLO. Inherited20point frontier is diagnostic only.
plan.hypothesis: In the prior mixed-budget burst32 of40 short requests finished before first capacity preemption; the two legal near-budget candidates were already spared by native tail. Reusing the original0.2s cadence tests whether continued arrivals alter this completion-versus-pressure ordering under normal capacity.
plan.claim_ceiling: One development workload characterization, not independent confirmation, a causal alternate-victim trajectory, application quality, or policy benefit. Only external arrival timing changes; same prompt content/order,40/280 caps, GPU/host/seed/warmup and all runtime mechanisms. A lack of pressure is a valid normal-capacity boundary. Declared remaining budget does not predict natural EOS.
plan.retention: Preserve all burst results/failures. One new spread-arrival tail cell; no automatic restart or adaptive arrival-rate scan.
plan.simple_comparators: Diagnostic ordinary max remaining declared budget, tie latest suffix index, plus same-held/computed-pages restricted version. Neither is a full CacheOPT implementation or actual alternate trajectory.

plan.diagnostic_question: At an existing0.2s external cadence, does normal-capacity pressure coexist with near-budget tail requests and legal alternative victims?
plan.decision_rule: One cell only. With real pressure and previously absent near-completion legal tail alternatives, next test a bounded real intervention. native_victim_observation.mapping_semantics: computed_tokens and both host fields come directly from candidate rows; absent values stay UNKNOWN. No fallback to output limits or later events.

pending_native_store_dependencies.semantics: Registered native STORE dependencies only; None includes missing/invalid mapping or non-STORE jobs. Repeated candidate observations are not independent. No DMA duration or exposed wait is measured.

observed_cpu_cost.semantics: candidate_observation_wall_s includes host, pending-dependency and progress-field reads and is contained in selector_wall_s. Do not sum the two. Separate host/pending timing is NOT_RECORDED.

actual_release.semantics: Exact step + internal request ID joins only. Released capacity is the free-pool counter difference around the native preempt call; its method duration excludes later native flush and is not DMA wait.

least_generated_shadow.semantics: Read-only suffix shadow: minimum produced output_tokens, then latest suffix index; any original unqualified suffix state falls back to native tail. This only checks whether the simple ranking remains equivalent on each executed trajectory, not its unrun end-to-end outcome.

native_selection_differences.semantics: Selected-minus-tail fields compare pre-action candidates in the same executed decision. actual_released_blocks reuses the exact decision_index release join. Actual release minus counterfactual tail held pages is NOT a measured causal difference between two releases: tail was not executed when selection changed, and held pages are only a release proxy. Extra released capacity remains a confound of any host-signal benefit. Aggregates are dependent changed-event descriptions, not independent repeats; unknown fields remain unknown.

executed_choice_check.semantics: Executed rule recomputation uses the recorded original qualification and protection/phase guards. Raw host-missing shadows are not host_near decisions.

measured_capacity.semantics: Physical allocation includes the null page; pin this exact byte budget in all policy cells.

arrival_submission_and_drain.semantics: admission_s marks the start of synchronous engine.add_request, so admission minus external arrival is client submission lag, not native queue waiting or scheduler admission. engine_add_return minus admission is host call duration. Failed and unfinished are exact raw status counts; other statuses remain in status_counts. No separate exhaustive rejection or per-request timeout counter exists in this raw schema; they remain UNKNOWN and are not inferred from failed. runtime_limit is a capture-level stop, not an individual timeout classification. Last observed completion is not full drain unless the entire planned cohort completed; request drain does not assert connector/KV cleanup completion.

victim_next_admission.semantics: First later residency admission with the same internal request ID, not a reconstructed load event. Next held pages below the earlier ready prefix rules out retaining that full prefix in GPU capacity at this admission; actual cache hits, recomputation, and copy cost remain UNKNOWN. Decision-to-admission includes queueing and native load waiting; admission-to-next-output also includes ordinary scheduling. Neither interval isolates transfer cost.

native_event_outcomes.semantics: Decision clock is host_perf_counter_s minus measurement origin. The next output is the first strictly later host-return output event, with both engine ordinal at selection and next cumulative host output recorded. These are absolute observed waits, not incremental effects; failed_request is only a prospective beneficiary, may self-preempt, and is not a funding target. No cross-run event match or imputation after EOS.

outputs.semantics: Reported stop is not assumed to mean EOS. EOS tokens may be omitted by the engine; emitted final EOS IDs are only direct observations.

remaining_budget_shadows.semantics: Development opportunity diagnosis on one synthetic budget-mixture tail run. Shadows describe alternatives at observed tail states; they were not executed and are not same-state causal comparisons, predictions of completion benefit, or gains versus uniform-budget runs. One KV page is a descriptive token count, not an application SLO. Decisions are not independent repeats.
